overview: Dual-Solver introduces a learned predictor-corrector ODE solver for diffusion models with three learnable parameter families (γ for prediction type interpolation, τ for log-linear domain change, κ for residual adjustment), optimized via a classification-based objective using pretrained classifiers, achieving state-of-the-art FID and CLIP scores in the low-NFE regime across diffusion and flow-matching backbones.

modules.name: Diffusion Noise Schedule
modules.description: Compute signal rate αt, noise rate σt, and half log-SNR λt = log(αt/σt) for various schedule types including variance-preserving (VP), variance-exploding (VE), and optimal transport (OT), along with their time derivatives needed for ODE formulation.

modules.name: Prediction Type Conversion
modules.description: Implement bidirectional conversion between noise prediction ϵθ, data prediction xθ, and velocity prediction vθ using the algebraic relationships in Eq. 4, enabling any backbone to provide dual predictions regardless of its training objective.

modules.name: Dual Prediction Formulation
modules.description: Implement the γ-parameterized integral and differential forms of dual prediction (Eqs. 5 and 11), which continuously interpolate among noise prediction (γ=-1), velocity prediction (γ=0), and data prediction (γ=1), computing coefficients A, B, C, D for both γ≥0 and γ<0 branches.

modules.name: Log-Linear Domain Transform
modules.description: Implement the log-linear domain change function L(y; τ) = log(1+τy)/τ (Eq. 8), its inverse L⁻¹(u; τ) = (e^{τu}-1)/τ, and the derivative dL⁻¹/du = e^{τu}, along with the variable transformations u(t) and v(t) from Eq. 6 that map the integrands of the dual prediction integral into the transformed domain.

modules.name: Approximation and Residual Terms
modules.description: Implement the residual adjustment function K(∆u; κ) = κ(∆u)² and compute the finite-difference approximations for xθ and ϵθ in the transformed domain, including first-order (constant), second-order forward-difference, and second-order backward-difference expansions, along with the weighted integral ∆L⁻¹ terms.

modules.name: First-Order Predictor
modules.description: Implement the first-order predictor update equation (Eq. 9) that combines the current state x_{t_i} with constant approximations of xθ and ϵθ in the transformed domain, incorporating the residual terms K(∆u; κ_u) and K(∆v; κ_v).

modules.name: Second-Order Corrector
modules.description: Implement the second-order corrector update equation (Eq. 10) that refines the predictor output using second-order forward-difference approximations of xθ and ϵθ, combining evaluations at both t_i and t_{i+1} to achieve O((∆t)³) local truncation error.

modules.name: Second-Order Predictor
modules.description: Implement the second-order predictor update equation (Eq. 12) using second-order backward-difference approximations of xθ and ϵθ with the step-size ratio r_i, primarily used for ablation studies comparing predictor-corrector configurations.

modules.name: Dual-Solver Sampling Loop
modules.description: Implement the full predictor-corrector sampling procedure (Algorithm 1), managing the list of previous model evaluations, iterating through timesteps, applying the first-order predictor followed by the second-order corrector at each step, and skipping the corrector at the final step.

modules.name: Learnable Parameter Manager
modules.description: Define and manage all per-step learnable parameters: predictor parameters ϕ_pred = {γ_pred, τ_u^pred, τ_v^pred, κ_u^pred, κ_v^pred} and corrector parameters ϕ_corr = {γ_corr, τ_u^corr, τ_v^corr, κ_u^corr, κ_v^corr}, handling the parameter-sharing and fixing configurations needed for ablation studies.

modules.name: Learnable Timestep Schedule
modules.description: Implement the learnable timestep scheduling with unnormalized step variables ∆t'_i and softmax normalization to produce non-negative step sizes summing to one, then computing timesteps via cumulative sum with fixed t_0 and t_M endpoints, enabling end-to-end gradient flow through the schedule.

modules.name: Classification-Based Learning Objective
modules.description: Implement the hard-label classification objective (Algorithm 2) that computes cross-entropy loss between a pretrained classifier's output on generated samples and the input class labels, and the soft-label classification variant that matches teacher solver classifier outputs, both enabling gradient backpropagation through the solver parameters.

modules.name: Regression-Based Learning Objective
modules.description: Implement trajectory regression, sample regression, and feature regression (LPIPS-based) objectives that compare student solver outputs against teacher solver targets, supporting the comparison experiments in the ablation study.

modules.name: Training Pipeline
modules.description: Implement the full training workflow including the AdamW optimizer with cosine annealing learning rate schedule, batch processing of noise-condition pairs, gradient computation through the sampling loop and classifier, and parameter updates for all solver parameters and timestep schedule.

modules.name: Evaluation Metrics
modules.description: Implement FID score computation using reference dataset statistics and CLIP score computation as cosine similarity between text and image features, supporting both ImageNet class-conditional and text-to-image evaluation protocols on 50k and 30k sample sizes respectively.

modules.name: Ablation Study Framework
modules.description: Implement configuration-driven ablation experiments covering predictor-corrector configurations (p1, p1c2, p2, p2c2), parameter fixation settings (γ fixed, τ fixed, κ fixed, shared), domain change function comparison (Type 1 linear interpolation vs. Type 2 log-linear), classifier selection study, and parameter learning method comparison.

modules.name: Cross-NFE Parameter Interpolation
modules.description: Implement linear interpolation (Definition G.1) and averaged linear interpolation (Definition G.2) for transferring learned parameter arrays across different NFE settings, enabling parameter reuse without retraining by interpolating between neighboring NFE configurations.
